title: Home Instruction
before:
Maine parents may choose to educate their children at home. Parents take full responsibility for the child while providing home instruction — they legally direct the child's education by choosing the curriculum, facilitating the process, and determining academic needs. Home instruction is funded exclusively by the parent.

Resources for Families

While the Department does not make curriculum recommendations, there are resources available for those interested in home instruction in Maine.

  • Check with your resident school administrative unit before the start of the school year regarding borrowing textbooks, unit assessments, and other public school resources.
  • Explore Maine's Content Areas and Standards to inform your teaching curriculum choices.
  • Connect with other home instruction parents and groups — many have an online presence or can be found through parent groups.
  • Read the Home Instruction Frequently Asked Questions.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 1 row holds two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 2.2× — 605 characters beside 269. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 2 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 2 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
